genZNote: As few as 10-50 organisms can make you sick — which is exactly why it's a Tier 1 select agent and not something you culture casually.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Wild rabbits, rodents, and other small mammals; ticks and deer flies serve as vectors
habitat.hostAssociation: Zoonotic — rabbits and rodents are the primary reservoir, with tick/deer fly bites as key transmission routes
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Can also survive in contaminated water, soil, and carcasses
habitat.reservoir: Rabbits, rodents, ticks, and deer flies

microscopy.stain: Gram stain (stains poorly); direct fluorescent antibody testing preferred

culture.media: Cysteine-enriched media (e.g., chocolate agar with added cysteine, or BCYE agar)
culture.growthCharacteristics: Obligate aerobe; fastidious, requires cysteine/cystine supplementation and BSL-3 handling due to extreme infectivity
culture.colonyMorphology: Small, gray-white, opaque colonies after 2-4 days

identificationClues: Tiny, faintly staining Gram-negative coccobacillus requiring cysteine-enriched media to grow
Extremely low infectious dose — as few as 10-50 organisms can cause disease via inhalation
Ulceroglandular presentation (skin ulcer with regional lymphadenopathy) is the most common clinical form
Classified as a Tier 1 Select Agent/potential bioterrorism agent due to its high infectivity

diseases: Tularemia ('rabbit fever') — ulceroglandular form most common (skin ulcer at inoculation site with tender regional lymphadenopathy); also pneumonic, oculoglandular, oropharyngeal, and typhoidal forms
virulenceFactors: Extremely low infectious dose contributing to high infectivity via aerosol
clinicalImportance.transmission: Tick or deer fly bites, direct contact with infected animal tissue (e.g., skinning rabbits), inhalation of contaminated aerosols/dust, or ingestion of contaminated water/undercooked meat
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Endemic in parts of North America, Europe, and Asia; a recognized potential bioterrorism agent due to its extreme infectivity via the aerosol route, prompting Tier 1 Select Agent classification
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Laboratory personnel must be alerted before processing suspected Francisella specimens — routine bench manipulation poses a serious aerosol infection risk, and cultures should be handled under BSL-3 conditions

examFacts.importantDisease: Tularemia (rabbit fever) — ulceroglandular form most common
examFacts.importantTest: Serology; culture only in a BSL-3 laboratory alerted in advance
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: One of the most infectious bacteria known (as few as 10-50 organisms), transmitted from rabbits/rodents via ticks, and a recognized Tier 1 bioterrorism agent
